evidence: NOT A CLONE (the defect the row names): HireOps is authored for its product. (1) Template placeholders are all replaced with product-specific values: task.toml name 'turing/hireops-recruiting-operations', description, difficulty_explanation, provenance, arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations'; template instruction.md 'CHANGE_ME' replaced by a HireOps brief; grep over the frozen task for CHANGE_ME/TODO/lorem/acme and for every sibling product name (pellmoor, threadline, torquebay, docketlight, bazaar, colderwater, ridgeline, gridforge, patchpad, medcare, drawbill, coursemark, oriel, expenseflow, 'vacanc') returns no hits. (2) Product-specific substance: hireops_rules.md defines a Kanban board with manual per-stage ordering shared by everyone (sec 3 'Order inside a stage'), per-job interview places 1-50, hiring-manager authority limited to Interview/Offer/Hired of own jobs, reject/reopen-to-origin with reason, versioned cards with 409 naming the colleague, optimistic move with put-back and focus retention, all-or-none multi-stage bulk move with board-order arrival, per-person single-level undo invalidated by later touches, live updates within 15 s that must not disturb typing/focus/open card/scroll (sec 5), staff-candidate conversations with 30-message paging that keeps the anchor, per-person unread, 'seen' rules that exclude the observer, per-person per-conversation drafts that survive session expiry and are hidden from other sign-ins (sec 6), and a candidate portal with its own status wording table and a strict no-leak list (sec 7). Seed: 3 jobs (Platform Engineer, Data Analyst, Product Designer), 16 applications, 127 messages incl. a 120-message conversation, read markers. Criteria ids are all hro_* and map to these mechanics (e.g. hro_reorder, hro_undo_once, hro_thread_earlier, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen, hro_drafts, hro_candidate_private, hro_pol_session_resume). (3) Sibling comparison. Closest same-domain sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (hiring). Its defining mechanics are interview panels of >=2 distinct people, 1-5 scores, assessment versioning invalidated by panel changes/reopen, frozen stages, a d3 funnel derived from stage history with loss attribution, vacancy openings reserved/filled by offer/hired, previewed batch offers, and idempotent actor-scoped retries/replays (its criteria: exact_derived_funnel, panel_change_invalidates_entire_assessment, successful_retry_replays_one_result, seeded_capacity_and_hired_offer_conversion, ...). None of those appear in HireOps; none of HireOps' manual ordering, undo, non-disruptive live board, conversations/unread/seen/drafts, or candidate portal appear in Pellmoor. Closest messaging sibling projects/threadline-chat is a Slack-style channel/thread/reaction/pin/webhook/presence product; HireOps' conversations are one-per-application staff-candidate threads with role-scoped access and candidate privacy, sharing only generic chat ideas (load older without jumping, per-user unread). Stage names, flows, roles, accounts and criteria differ; this is not a renamed copy of either. WHY NOTE AND RISK=TRUE: (a) Real conceptual overlap with Pellmoor in the same recruiting domain: stage-by-stage moves with skip refused (Pellmoor hiring-rules.md:1-3 'Do not skip stages'; HireOps hireops_rules.md sec 3 'Skipping a stage is refused'), a per-job capacity limit that refuses overfilling (vacancy openings vs interview places), all-or-none batch movement, stale-revision refusal, an activity trail, and a near-identical duplicate rule (Pellmoor hiring-rules.md:11-12 'The same person may apply for different roles, but must not appear twice against one vacancy.' vs hireops_rules.md:32-33 'the same address cannot be added to the same job twice ...; the same person may apply to different jobs'). These are natural recruiting rules, not copied flows, but a client reviewing both tasks would see two recruiting pipelines with refused-skip/capacity/batch/stale rules. (b) The row also asks whether the task fits 'the suite's domain plan'. No suite domain plan or assignment list exists in the workspace sources I could find (NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md only says 'author distinct domain behavior. Do not make nouns-swapped clones'; task.toml provenance says 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task', but the supplied source/assignment is not in the workspace; no other file outside qc/ and the task mentions HireOps except deliverables/.../REVIEW_STATUS.md and scripts/hireops_qc_rows.py, which I did not read as they are prior QC history). Whether Pellmoor and HireOps are delivered into the same suite slice, and whether the plan permits two recruiting tasks, is therefore unverified. Pellmoor's arena_slice ('full-stack-typescript-d3-esbuild-express-sqlite-pipeline') differs from HireOps' ('recruiting-hiring-operations'), which suggests distinct slices but does not prove plan fit. No runtime evidence is relevant to this row; raw-evidence-index.json was not used. App-level counterexamples (weak app passing / conforming app failing) do not apply to this authorship row: it grades the task's originality, not a submission.
suggested_fix: No task edit required for distinctness. Owner should confirm with the lead/assignment record that HireOps (arena_slice recruiting-hiring-operations) is the assigned domain and that Pellmoor is not in the same delivery suite (or that two recruiting tasks are acceptable); optionally reword the duplicate-application sentence in hireops_rules.md sec 2 so it does not echo Pellmoor's phrasing.
